precepts.text: Life hangs in doubt, fearing day and night, wishing morning were evening and evening were morning.
precepts.point: His flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust; his skin is broken and become loathsome. Satan smote him in his skin, and his flesh was covered in boils, pus, and worms.

note.label: Job 7: Job's Anguish and the Shortness of His Days

precepts.why:
Job says, “When I lie down, I say, When shall I arise, and the night be gone? and I am full of tossings to and fro unto the dawning of the day.” His spirit is in such anguish he cannot rest. That is the tossing of Deuteronomy 28: “And thy life shall hang in doubt before thee; and thou shalt fear day and night, and shalt have none assurance of thy life”.

Life hangs in doubt, fearing day and night, wishing morning were evening and evening were morning. When it is day Job wishes it were night, and when it is night he wishes it were day. Satan smote him in his skin, and his flesh was covered in boils, pus, and worms, “clothed with worms and clods of dust”, with months of vanity and wearisome nights appointed to him.

points: God visits a man every morning and tries him every moment: every second is a test, and a good day is often a test you failed to see.

note.label: The Art of War - Rules of Engagement

points: Job could not even swallow his spit before the next trial, and Satan tests you in your sleep too; you are a mark against him and a burden to yourself, and some fall away under that burden.

note.label: The Art of War - Rules of Engagement

points: What shall I do unto thee, O thou preserver of men? Why hast thou set me as a mark against thee, so that I am a burden to myself? Come on.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows

points: And why dost thou not pardon my transgression? So Job was praying, why do you not pardon my transgression, Lord?
And take away mine iniquity. And take away mine iniquity. Uh-oh. For now shall I sleep in the dust; and thou shalt seek me in the morning, but I shall not be.

points: Are not his days also like the days of an hireling? Meaning a dispensation of time is given to every man on this earth.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

points: As an hireling looketh for the reward of his work: a hireling generally looks for the reward of his work. That's what he's looking for.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

points: Is there not an appointed time to man upon earth, and are not his days like the days of a hireling? A hireling is a laborer who works for wages, a wage earner or paid servant who does his job and gets paid, no strings attached.

note.label: Job 7: Job's Anguish and the Shortness of His Days

points: As a servant earnestly desires the shadow, and a hireling looks for the reward of his work, so man's life is short. We come and then we go; we are here one day and gone the next.

note.label: Job 7: Job's Anguish and the Shortness of His Days

points: Job is made to possess months of vanity, and wearisome nights are appointed to him. When he lies down he asks when he shall arise, and he is full of tossing to and fro until the dawning of the day. His spirit is in such anguish he cannot rest.

note.label: Job 7: Job's Anguish and the Shortness of His Days

points: This is the tossing of Deuteronomy 28: when it is day he wishes it were night, and when it is night he wishes it were day.

note.label: Job 7: Job's Anguish and the Shortness of His Days

points: His flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust; his skin is broken and become loathsome. Satan smote him in his skin, and his flesh was covered in boils, pus, and worms.

note.label: Job 7: Job's Anguish and the Shortness of His Days

points: His days are swifter than a weaver's shuttle and spent without hope; his life is wind, and his eyes shall see no more good.

note.label: Job 7: Job's Anguish and the Shortness of His Days

points: The eye that has seen him shall see him no more; as the cloud is consumed and vanishes, so he that goes down to the grave shall come up no more, nor return to his house.

note.label: Job 7: Job's Anguish and the Shortness of His Days

points: Therefore Job will not refrain his mouth; he will speak in the anguish of his spirit and complain in the bitterness of his soul. He asks if he is a sea or a whale that God sets a watch over him.

note.label: Job 7: Job's Anguish and the Shortness of His Days

points: When he says his bed shall comfort him and his couch shall ease his complaint, then God scares him with dreams and terrifies him through visions, so his soul chooses strangling and death rather than life.

note.label: Job 7: Job's Anguish and the Shortness of His Days

points: Job loathes his life and would not live always; he asks to be let alone, for his days are vanity. What is man that God should magnify him, set His heart upon him, visit him every morning, and try him every moment?

note.label: Job 7: Job's Anguish and the Shortness of His Days

points: How long will God not depart from him, nor let him alone till he swallows down his spittle? Job feels so tried that he cannot even swallow his own spit without being afflicted.

note.label: Job 7: Job's Anguish and the Shortness of His Days

points: Job asks what he shall do if he has sinned, calling God the preserver of men, and why he is set as a mark and made a burden to himself.

note.label: Job 7: Job's Anguish and the Shortness of His Days

points: Why does God not pardon his transgression and take away his iniquity, for soon he shall sleep in the dust and be sought in the morning but not be found?
